stem: An analytics role in account B needs to read objects in an S3 bucket that account A owns. The role's identity-based policy in account B already allows s3:GetObject on the bucket's objects, but requests are still denied. Without sharing any long-term credentials, what should the data team in account A add?

choices.text: An SCP in account A's organization that allows the account B role to call s3:GetObject on the bucket
A permissions boundary on account A's administrator role that includes s3:GetObject for the account B role
A new IAM user in account A with S3 read access, created for the analytics team in account B
A bucket policy that allows s3:GetObject on the bucket's objects for the account B role's ARN

rationale: For a request from one account to another, the requester needs an identity-based policy in its own account and the resource-based policy in the owning account must also allow it. The role already has the first half, so account A adds a bucket policy that names the role and allows s3:GetObject. An SCP never grants permissions; it only limits the maximum permissions of principals in member accounts. A permissions boundary on another role in account A does not grant anything to the account B role and only caps the entity it is set on. An IAM user in account A would need access keys handed to account B, which are the long-term credentials the team must not share.
